statements.label: supported
statements.text: FOS/JUN, also called AP-1, are broadly expressed growth-factor-inducible transcription factors with a central role in choosing which enhancers cells use.
statements.evidence: the broadly expressed, growth-factor-inducible TFs FOS/JUN (AP-1) play a central role in enhancer selection.
statements.note: The abstract names FOS/JUN (AP-1) as broadly expressed, growth-factor-inducible factors central to enhancer selection.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: The same FOS/JUN and BAF mechanism selects enhancers in neurons just as it does in fibroblasts.
statements.evidence: We used a genetic approach to identify transcription factors (TFs) required for enhancer selection in fibroblasts.
statements.note: The study examined only fibroblasts and never extends the mechanism to neurons.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: To differentiate, cells pick out the thousands of active enhancers they need from roughly a million enhancers encoded across the genome.
statements.evidence: select from among the ∼10 6 enhancers encoded in the genome the thousands of enhancers that drive the gene programs that impart their distinct features
statements.note: The abstract says cells select thousands of enhancers from the roughly one million encoded genome-wide.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: FOS/JUN bind nucleosomal enhancers with cell-type-specific factors and recruit the SWI/SNF (BAF) complex, which increases chromatin accessibility.
statements.evidence: collaboratively binding to nucleosomal enhancers and recruiting the SWI/SNF (BAF) chromatin remodeling complex to establish accessible chromatin.
statements.note: The abstract describes FOS/JUN recruiting BAF to nucleosomal enhancers to establish accessible chromatin.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: In differentiating neurons, ACSS2 builds up in the nucleus at upregulated genes near sites of strong histone acetylation.
statements.evidence: ACSS2 increases in the nuclei of differentiating neurons and localizes to upregulated neuronal genes near sites of elevated histone acetylation.
statements.note: The abstract reports ACSS2 accumulating in nuclei at upregulated genes near elevated histone acetylation.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Cutting ACSS2 levels lowered nuclear acetyl-CoA, histone acetylation, and the stimulus-driven expression of the neuronal gene cohort.
statements.evidence: A decrease in ACSS2 lowers nuclear acetyl-CoA levels, histone acetylation, and responsive expression of the cohort of neuronal genes.
statements.note: The abstract states lowering ACSS2 reduces acetyl-CoA, histone acetylation, and responsive neuronal gene expression.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: Boosting ACSS2 activity reverses age-related memory decline in mice.
statements.evidence: attenuation of hippocampal ACSS2 expression impairs long-term spatial memory, a cognitive process that relies on histone acetylation.
statements.note: The study only lowers ACSS2 and never tests raising it or any effect on aging.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: In adult mice, knocking down hippocampal ACSS2 impaired long-term spatial memory, which depends on histone acetylation.
statements.evidence: attenuation of hippocampal ACSS2 expression impairs long-term spatial memory, a cognitive process that relies on histone acetylation.
statements.note: The abstract reports that reducing hippocampal ACSS2 impairs long-term spatial memory.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: Enhancer-promoter looping at this locus relies on the cohesin complex.
statements.evidence: We show that sustained proximity of the enhancer to its target is required for activation.
statements.note: The abstract shows proximity is needed for activation but never identifies cohesin or any factor mediating the interaction.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: The study resolved three distinct topological conformations at the locus and measured how quickly it transitions between them.
statements.evidence: we identify three distinct topological conformation states and measure their transition kinetics.
statements.note: The abstract reports three topological conformation states with measured transition kinetics.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Transcription feeds back on topology, as it enhances the temporal stability of the proximal conformation and coincides with further spatial compaction.
statements.evidence: it enhances the temporal stability of the proximal conformation and is associated with further spatial compaction.
statements.note: The abstract states transcription enhances the stability of the proximal conformation and is linked to further compaction.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: The reporter switched on only when the enhancer stayed close to its target promoter for a sustained period.
statements.evidence: We show that sustained proximity of the enhancer to its target is required for activation.
statements.note: The abstract states sustained enhancer-target proximity is required for activation.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: By shielding cohesin from loop release, CTCF promotes the formation of chromatin loops.
statements.evidence: CTCF enables the formation of chromatin loops by protecting cohesin against loop release.
statements.note: The abstract concludes CTCF enables chromatin-loop formation by protecting cohesin against loop release.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: A 2.7 Å crystal structure of the SA2-SCC1 subunits bound to CTCF revealed the molecular basis of their interaction.
statements.evidence: We report a crystal structure of SA2-SCC1 in complex with CTCF at a resolution of 2.7 Å, which reveals the molecular basis of the interaction.
statements.note: The abstract reports a 2.7 Å crystal structure of SA2-SCC1 bound to CTCF.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: A segment in the CTCF N terminus makes contact with the SA2-SCC1 subunits of human cohesin.
statements.evidence: a segment within the CTCF N terminus interacts with the SA2-SCC1 subunits of human cohesin.
statements.note: The abstract shows a CTCF N-terminal segment interacts with the SA2-SCC1 cohesin subunits.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: The CTCF-cohesin interaction is disrupted in cancers with chromosomal instability.
statements.evidence: These results provide fundamental insights into the molecular mechanism that enables the dynamic regulation of chromatin folding by cohesin and CTCF.
statements.note: The abstract is structural and mechanistic and never discusses disease or cancer.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Without CTCF, cohesin is misrouted away from CTCF sites and gathers at the transcription start sites of active genes.
statements.evidence: cohesin cannot be properly recruited to CTCF sites but instead accumulates at transcription start sites of active genes
statements.note: The abstract reports that in CTCF-depleted cells cohesin accumulates at transcription start sites instead of CTCF sites.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Altering gene expression shifts where these 'cohesin islands' sit along the genome.
statements.evidence: Changing gene expression modulates the position of these 'cohesin islands'.
statements.note: The abstract states changing gene expression repositions the cohesin islands.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Loss of both CTCF and Wapl lets cohesin build up in regions as long as 70 kilobases at the 3' ends of active genes.
statements.evidence: In the absence of both CTCF and Wapl, cohesin accumulates in up to 70 kilobase-long regions at 3'-ends of active genes
statements.note: The abstract reports cohesin accumulating in up to 70-kilobase regions at 3' ends when both CTCF and Wapl are absent.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: Cohesin islands at convergent gene 3' ends interfere with transcription termination.
statements.evidence: cohesin accumulates in up to 70 kilobase-long regions at 3'-ends of active genes, in particular if these converge on each other
statements.note: The abstract reports where islands form but never addresses any effect on transcription termination.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: By blocking transcription termination, the IAV NS1 protein triggers readthrough transcription extending for hundreds of kilobases past gene ends.
statements.evidence: global inhibition of transcription termination by IAV NS1 protein causes readthrough transcription for hundreds of kilobases.
statements.note: The abstract states NS1-driven termination inhibition causes readthrough transcription for hundreds of kilobases.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: IAV readthrough transcription permanently alters the host epigenome after the infection clears.
statements.evidence: during influenza A (IAV) infection, rampant transcription rapidly reorganizes host cell chromatin interactions.
statements.note: The abstract describes changes during infection but never addresses whether they persist afterward.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: When elongation is blocked, cohesin instead builds up at intragenic CTCF sites and promotes chromatin looping and compaction.
statements.evidence: inhibition of transcription elongation allows cohesin to accumulate at previously transcribed intragenic CTCF sites and to mediate chromatin looping and compaction.
statements.note: The abstract reports that blocking elongation lets cohesin accumulate at intragenic CTCF sites and mediate looping and compaction.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: In readthrough regions, elongating RNA polymerase II displaces cohesin from CTCF sites, disrupting chromatin interactions and decompacting the locus.
statements.evidence: elongating RNA polymerase II disrupts chromatin interactions by inducing cohesin displacement from CTCF sites, leading to locus decompaction.
statements.note: The abstract reports elongating Pol II displaces cohesin from CTCF sites, disrupting interactions and decompacting the locus.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: The H3K4me3Q5ser mark appears across mammalian tissues, with the strongest presence in brain and gut.
statements.evidence: H3K4me3Q5ser displays a ubiquitous pattern of tissue expression in mammals, with enrichment observed in brain and gut
statements.note: The abstract reports ubiquitous H3K4me3Q5ser expression with enrichment in brain and gut.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: H3K4me3Q5ser nucleosomes are enriched in euchromatin, respond to differentiation, and track with permissive gene expression.
statements.evidence: H3K4me3Q5ser nucleosomes are enriched in euchromatin, are sensitive to cellular differentiation and correlate with permissive gene expression
statements.note: The abstract reports H3K4me3Q5ser nucleosomes enriched in euchromatin and correlating with permissive expression.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: Serotonin reuptake inhibitors raise H3Q5ser levels in the brains of patients with depression.
statements.evidence: these data identify a direct role for 5-HT, independent from its contributions to neurotransmission and cellular signalling, in the mediation of permissive gene expression.
statements.note: The abstract defines a chromatin role for serotonin but never addresses SSRIs, depression, or patients.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Tissue transglutaminase 2 adds serotonin to H3K4me3-marked nucleosomes, producing the combinatorial mark H3K4me3Q5ser in vivo.
statements.evidence: tissue transglutaminase 2 can serotonylate histone H3 tri-methylated lysine 4 (H3K4me3)-marked nucleosomes, resulting in the presence of combinatorial H3K4me3Q5ser in vivo.
statements.note: The abstract reports transglutaminase 2 serotonylating H3K4me3 nucleosomes to form H3K4me3Q5ser in vivo.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Across hundreds of cell lines, an enhancer's transcriptional effect depended on its contact probability with the promoter in a nonlinear way.
statements.evidence: A quantitative analysis of hundreds of cell lines reveals that the transcriptional effect of an enhancer depends on its contact probabilities with the promoter through a nonlinear relationship.
statements.note: The abstract reports a nonlinear dependence of enhancer effect on contact probability across hundreds of cell lines.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Enhancer strength set not only absolute transcription levels but also how readily a promoter could be insulated by CTCF.
statements.evidence: enhancer strength also determines absolute transcription levels as well as the sensitivity of a promoter to CTCF-mediated transcriptional insulation.
statements.note: The abstract states enhancer strength determines absolute transcription levels and sensitivity to CTCF insulation.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: The nonlinear enhancer-promoter relationship is conserved between mammals and Drosophila.
statements.evidence: Chromosome structure in mammals is thought to regulate transcription by modulating three-dimensional interactions between enhancers and promoters
statements.note: The study concerns mammalian cells only and never compares other species.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Modelling proposed that transient enhancer-promoter contacts are translated into slower promoter bursting within individual cells.
statements.evidence: transient enhancer-promoter interactions being translated into slower promoter bursting dynamics in individual cells
statements.note: The abstract's modelling links transient enhancer-promoter contacts to slower promoter bursting in single cells.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: A longer cohesin depletion of 24 hours would abolish enhancer-promoter interactions.

statements.evidence: live-cell, single-molecule imaging revealed that cohesin depletion reduced transcription factor (TF) binding to chromatin.
statements.note: The abstract reports that cohesin depletion reduced TF binding, seen by single-molecule imaging.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: A brief 3-hour depletion of CTCF, cohesin, or WAPL left enhancer-promoter interactions largely unchanged.
statements.evidence: enhancer-promoter (E-P) interactions are largely insensitive to acute (3-h) depletion of CTCF, cohesin or WAPL.
statements.note: The abstract reports E-P interactions largely insensitive to acute 3-hour depletion of CTCF, cohesin, or WAPL.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Acute removal of YY1 also had minimal impact on enhancer-promoter loops, transcription, and 3D genome folding.
statements.evidence: acute YY1 depletion also had minimal effects on E-P loops, transcription and 3D genome folding.
statements.note: The abstract reports acute YY1 depletion had minimal effects on E-P loops, transcription, and folding.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Stripping away H3K27me3 from these normally paternally expressed genes switched on expression from the maternal allele.
statements.evidence: these genes are paternally expressed in preimplantation embryos, and ectopic removal of H3K27me3 induces maternal allele expression.
statements.note: The abstract states removing H3K27me3 induces expression from the maternal allele of these paternally expressed genes.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: H3K27me3-based imprinting was largely lost in the embryonic lineage, yet five genes kept their imprinted expression in the extra-embryonic lineage.

statements.note: The abstract reports imprinting largely lost in the embryonic lineage but maintained for at least five genes extra-embryonically.
